newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE coffee pulls back further from 9-mth peak.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE coffee pulls back further from 9-mth peak.

text.p: LIFFE coffee futures stepped back further from their early vault to a new nine-month peak to end Tuesday with pared gains on late trade selling.
Prices were earlier hammered by origin offers but good roaster buying at the lows helped keep values in the positive territory by the finish.
The benchmark May contract marched to a new nine-month peak of $1,825 a tonne soon after the opening bell in line with market expectations after a renewed surge in New York on Monday.

But the move to above $1,800 on thin volume was short-lived and pries gradually fell back to finish $51 up at $1,768. May last peaked at $1,820 on Wednesday. Technically, the contract faces stiff resistance at $1,820 and $1,860.
Volume was a modest 6,164 lots. Traders said the continued wild fluctuations in New York arabica futures continued to unnerve London.

Until Monday's renewed New York rally as news of a retail price hike by U.S. roaster Folgers coincided with specs' buy-stops, the market looked set to extend its downward correction to the prolonged bull run since the New Year.
"The market is so unpredictable at the moment...," said one trader. "There's no real resistance or support."
Fundamentally, retail price hikes would hurt consumption but analysts said the Folgers move is seen as a short-term bullish factor as it could lead to consumer hoarding.
New York's May continued to struggle above $2.00 on Tuesday after hitting a peak of 205.40 cents.
Traders said a close above 205 cents on Tuesday could signal further fund and general buying. But this could also make the market vulnerable to profit-taking as seen in the previous sessions.

In other news, the Association of Coffee Producing Countries said it would hold a technical meeting on March 20 in London to review the surge in coffee prices. --Jalil Hamid, London newsroom +44 171 542 4985
